chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who caught up with the Imam while he was sitting after the two prostrations (of the fourth rak'ah). He said: 'He begins the prayer (with Takbir) and does not sit with the Imam until he stands up.'

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: The two prostrations (or two rak'ahs, contextually the final sitting)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they join the prayer after the Imam has already sat for Tashahhud in the fourth rak'ah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural ruling for a latecomer (Ma'mum) who arrives after the Imam has completed the two prostrations of the fourth rak'ah and is in the sitting position (Jalsah). The Imam instructs that the latecomer should initiate their prayer independently by standing up to perform the remaining rak'ahs, rather than remaining seated with the Imam, ensuring the validity of their individual prayer component before joining the Imam's final standing. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the precise timing of joining the congregational prayer to maintain the structural integrity of the worship.
